html:
The Odrysian Kingdom was a Thracian state in the eastern Balkans, in today's Bulgaria, European Turkey and northern Greece. It was the first large state in the region, founded in the early 5th century BCE. On this map it appears in 1 BCE, near the end of its long life.

Thrace was a land of warlike tribes, famous for horsemen, gold and silver work. After the Persians withdrew from Europe, King Teres I united many tribes under the Odrysians. His son Sitalces made it a major power and allied with Athens in the Peloponnesian War. It had no fixed capital until Seuthes III built Seuthopolis in the late 4th century BCE.

Philip II of Macedon conquered much of it in the 340s BCE, and its power shrank. Thracian kings survived as clients, and by 1 BCE a Thracian kingdom was a client of Rome. In 46 CE the emperor Claudius annexed it as the Roman province of Thrace, part of the Roman Empire.
